title: Exploring the therapeutic potential of syringaldehyde in imiquimod-induced psoriasis model in mice via NF-kappaB pathway inhibition.
authors: Gosia, Meeral; Godad, Angel; Pahelkar, Akshata; Doshi, Gaurav
one_liner_zh: 该文研究丁香醛对银屑病小鼠模型的治疗作用，仅用分子对接评估小分子与NF-kappaB/MAPK蛋白的结合，未涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合机制，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Psoriasis is characterized by increased levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines, including TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, IL-17A, and NF-kappaB, as well as keratinocyte hyperproliferation and epidermal thickening. Its pathophysiology is significantly influenced by oxidative stress and abnormal activation of redox-sensitive signaling pathways, such as NF-kappaB and MAPK. The present study examined the potential of Syringaldehyde (SYD) in the imiquimod (IMQ) induced psoriasis model. Psoriasis Area Severity Index (PASI) scores, back skin thickness, and spleen hypertrophy decreased at dose levels of SYD 25, 50, and 100 mg/kg. Furthermore, a significant reduction in PASI scores following SYD administration indicated a marked improvement in the disease severity and lesion morphology. High-affinity binding of SYD to NF-kappaB (PDB ID: 4KIK; -34.76 kcal/mol) and MAPK (PDB ID: 1A9U; -32.87 kcal/mol) was found by molecular docking, indicating interference with nuclear translocation and phosphorylation processes. The treatment groups 50 mg/kg and 100 mg/kg indicated restoration of normal histological features. The biochemical evaluation showed decrease in NF-kappaB, IL-1beta, TNF-alpha, and IL-17 on treatment with SYD. Thus, SYD appears to be a potential therapeutic option for psoriasis, but additional research is needed to confirm its efficacy and safety.
abstract_zh: 银屑病以促炎细胞因子水平升高为特征，包括TNF-alpha、IL-1beta、IL-17A和NF-kappaB，以及角质形成细胞过度增殖和表皮增厚。其病理生理学显著受氧化应激和氧化还原敏感信号通路（如NF-kappaB和MAPK）异常激活的影响。本研究考察了丁香醛（Syringaldehyde, SYD）在咪喹莫特（imiquimod, IMQ）诱导的银屑病模型中的潜力。在SYD 25、50和100 mg/kg剂量水平下，银屑病面积严重程度指数（Psoriasis Area Severity Index, PASI）评分、背部皮肤厚度和脾脏肥大均有所降低。此外，SYD给药后PASI评分的显著降低表明疾病严重程度和病变形态明显改善。分子对接发现SYD与NF-kappaB（PDB ID: 4KIK；-34.76 kcal/mol）和MAPK（PDB ID: 1A9U；-32.87 kcal/mol）具有高亲和力结合，表明其干扰核转位和磷酸化过程。50 mg/kg和100 mg/kg治疗组显示正常组织学特征的恢复。生化评估显示，SYD治疗后NF-kappaB、IL-1beta、TNF-alpha和IL-17水平降低。因此，SYD似乎是银屑病的潜在治疗选择，但需要进一步研究以确认其有效性和安全性。
